welcome.headline: Your manager and the floor he runs
welcome.desc: {{godName}} is your office manager. He runs a small team of AI workers for you, and you watch it all from one screen. Here's what's inside:

team.label: Your starter team
team.desc: {{godName}} suggests a team suited to the kind of business you run. You pick who joins, and can add or remove anyone later.

manager.label: {{godName}} runs the floor
manager.desc: {{godName}}, your office manager, takes your requests, hands each job to the right team member, and only interrupts you when it matters.

memory.label: They remember
memory.desc: Your team remembers what you've told them and what they've already done, so you never have to explain things twice.

commandCenter.label: Everything in view
commandCenter.desc: One screen shows what everyone is working on, what's finished, and what's waiting for you.

guardrails.label: You stay in charge
guardrails.desc: Your team asks before posting online or anything that costs money, and sends email only the way you set it. You decide what they can do on their own.

hires.desc: Need another pair of hands? Add a team member in one click. No setup needed.

home.desc: Create a new, empty folder for the app to call home. Everything the app remembers (its own settings and your agents' memory) is stored here. Something like ~/HarnessAgents works well. We'll create it for you if it doesn't exist.
home.note: You won't need to open this folder day to day. It's just where the app keeps its notes, so nothing is lost when you restart.
home.syncWarningTitle: Don't put this in a synced folder
home.syncWarning: Keep it out of Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive and iCloud Drive, and out of Desktop or Documents if your computer backs those up to the cloud. The app writes here constantly, and syncing can corrupt your team's memory and break the link the app uses to keep them in check. The suggested ~/HarnessAgents is safe.

orchestrator.desc: {{godName}} is your office manager. He reads your requests, breaks them into tasks, and hands them to the right team member. He runs the floor; you own the business. He runs on Claude Code. Pick which Claude model he uses.
orchestrator.cliAgent: Claude Code, made by Anthropic, is the AI that powers your office. It runs right here on this computer. Your manager is always on and runs your whole office. We recommend Opus 5.5, the newest model.
orchestrator.workersOnlyHint: Can't drain hive mail yet, so it can't run your office. Still available when hiring workers.
orchestrator.modelNote: This sets the model {{godName}} and your whole team use. You can change it later in Settings.
orchestrator.maxPlan: You'll need a Claude Max plan to keep your office running full time. Smaller plans reach their usage limit during the day, and the office pauses until the limit resets.

permissions.autonomyHead: How much can agents do on their own?
permissions.autoLabel: Let agents work on their own
permissions.autoOn: On. Agents carry out tasks without stopping to ask, for the smoothest experience.
permissions.autoOff: Off. Agents pause and ask you before changing files or running commands.
permissions.autoNote: Best when agents work in their own projects. You can change this later, including for individual agents.
permissions.reliabilityHead: Keep things running while you're away
permissions.reliabilityDesc: Your agents keep working on a schedule and in live terminals, even when you step away. These settings keep you in the loop and keep things running.
permissions.keepAwakeDesc: Stops your computer from sleeping while an agent is live, so schedules and terminals fire on time even when you step away. Uses more battery, so it's best on power. Off by default.
permissions.notificationsDesc: {{godName}} pings you when something needs you, even while you're away. Your system may ask permission the first time.
permissions.openAtLoginDesc: Relaunch the harness after a reboot so scheduled missions resume on their own. No prompt; applies immediately.
permissions.shareStatsDesc: A handful of anonymous events (app opened, agent spawned, feature used) that help improve the app. Never prompts, code, file paths, or agent output. Full list in TELEMETRY.md; change anytime in Settings.
permissions.stayAwakeDescMac: macOS only lets you set this one yourself. In Battery → Options, turn on "Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off" (on power adapter) so timers keep firing with the display asleep. Without a setting that prevents sleep, the Mac still truly sleeps; work survives and catches up on wake.
permissions.stayAwakeDescWindows: Windows only lets you set this one yourself. In Settings → System → Power & battery → Screen, blank & sleep, set "On battery power, put my device to sleep" and "When plugged in" to Never (or increase them) so timers keep firing. Without a setting that prevents sleep, Windows still truly sleeps; work survives and catches up on wake.
permissions.stayAwakeDescLinux: Your desktop environment only lets you set this one yourself. Look for a Power Settings panel (for example GNOME Settings → Power, or KDE System Settings → Power Management) and turn off automatic sleep or suspend while on power. Without a setting that prevents sleep, your machine still truly sleeps; work survives and catches up on wake.

god.summary: {{name}} is your office manager and your one point of contact. The team reports to {{name}}, never to you: {{name}} hands out the work, relays the results, and brings you only what needs you.
does: Hands each job to the right team member, with what to send back
Answers small things right away: a quick fact, a short reply
Keeps the task board up to date, so it is right whenever you look
Checks on the team at each standup and gets anything stalled moving
Puts every question for you on Ask me, short, with options

A job nobody on the team covers: add someone, hand it over, do it once, or drop it

mailboxes.title: Mailboxes
mailboxes.intro: Mailboxes your team can work in. You choose who uses which one on each team member's Access tab.
mailboxes.empty: No mailboxes yet. Add sales@, support@ or your own inbox, then choose which team member works in it.

help.gmail: Gmail needs an app password, not your normal one. Turn on 2 Step Verification, then create one at myaccount.google.com/apppasswords.
help.google-workspace: Use an app password from myaccount.google.com/apppasswords. If that page is missing, your Workspace admin has turned app passwords off.
help.icloud: iCloud needs an app specific password. Create one at account.apple.com under Sign In and Security.
help.yahoo: Yahoo needs an app password. Create one in Account Security, then Generate app password.
help.zoho: Zoho needs an app specific password from Security, then App Passwords, with IMAP turned on in Mail settings.
help.other: Your email host lists these servers in its help pages. If your normal password is refused, ask them for an app password.
